title: Parameter constraints, identifiability and sensitivity
objective:
Identify model parameters, allowed domains, degeneracies and
identifiability questions. Specify what Bell-type observations could
constrain and what they cannot identify without extra assumptions.
Develop a reproducible numerical plan, including null models,
sensitivity analysis and uncertainty treatment. Do not report
invented fitted parameters or simulated empirical evidence.

deterministic_computations.interpretation: The local deterministic CHSH bound is exhaustively checked for the 16 deterministic assignments. The quantum singlet value is a numerical baseline. These checks do not establish a superdeterministic model or a new physical result.

## 1. Executive result  

| Item | Statement | Epistemic tag |
|------|-----------|---------------|
| **(E1)** | The *observable* CHSH combination  \(\mathcal{S}=E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}\)  is a linear functional of the four bipartite correlators \(E_{xy}\). Its value can be bounded **locally** by \(|\mathcal{S}|\le 2\) under the standard factorisation (Bell‑locality) assumptions. | **DERIVED** (standard Bell‑inequality proof) |
| **(E2)** | Within quantum mechanics the singlet state attains \(|\mathcal{S}|=2\sqrt2\) (Tsirelson bound). This value is reproduced by the baseline numerical check (Section “quantum_singlet_baseline”). | **SOURCE_SUPPORTED** (baseline) |
| **(E3)** | The *parameter set* \(\{p(\lambda),A_x(\lambda),B_y(\lambda)\}\) that defines a Bell‑local hidden‑variable (LHV) model is **highly non‑identifiable** from the four correlators alone: many distinct parameterisations generate exactly the same \(\{E_{xy}\}\). Only the *convex hull* of deterministic response assignments is observable. | **UNRESOLVED** (identifiability analysis) |
| **(E4)** | A *measurement‑dependent* (MD) model that relaxes the independence of \(\lambda\) from the settings \((x,y)\) can reproduce any set of correlators, including the Tsirelson value, **provided** one supplies an explicit joint distribution \(p(\lambda, x, y)\). Without an independent specification of this distribution the model is **unidentifiable** from Bell‑type data alone. | **CONDITIONAL** |
| **(E5)** | Sensitivity of the CHSH value to variations in the hidden‑variable distribution is linear: \(\delta\mathcal{S}= \sum_{\lambda} \delta p(\lambda)\, \mathcal{S}(\lambda)\) where \(\mathcal{S}(\lambda)=A_0(\lambda)B_0(\lambda)+A_0(\lambda)B_1(\lambda)+A_1(\lambda)B_0(\lambda)-A_1(\lambda)B_1(\lambda)\). The maximal magnitude of \(\mathcal{S}(\lambda)\) over deterministic assignments is 2 (see baseline). Hence any admissible perturbation of \(p(\lambda)\) can change \(\mathcal{S}\) by at most \(2\) in absolute value. | **COMPUTATIONALLY_CHECKED** (deterministic enumeration) |
| **(E6)** | A reproducible numerical plan is outlined (Section 8) that (i) enumerates the 16 deterministic response tables, (ii) samples arbitrary hidden‑variable distributions, (iii) evaluates \(\mathcal{S}\) and (iv) performs a finite‑difference sensitivity analysis. | **CONDITIONAL** (requires implementation) |

| \(y\in\{0,1\}\) | Bob’s measurement setting (binary) | \(\{0,1\}\) |
| \(a\in\{-1,+1\}\) | Alice’s outcome | \(\{-1,+1\}\) |
| \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) | Bob’s outcome | \(\{-1,+1\}\) |
| \(\lambda\) | Hidden variable (possibly vector‑valued) | Arbitrary measurable space \(\Lambda\) |

| \(B_y(\lambda)\) | Deterministic response function for Bob: \(B_y:\Lambda\to\{-1,+1\}\) | \(\{-1,+1\}\) |
| \(E_{xy}\) | Correlator \(\langle a b\rangle\) for setting pair \((x,y)\) | \([-1,1]\) |

| \(\mathcal{S}(\lambda)\) | Deterministic contribution of a single \(\lambda\) (see Eq. (5)) | \(\{-2,0,2\}\) for deterministic tables |
